findings.reason: a worker must either build a velocity invalidation path with no caller (dead code) or find the client re-request test unsatisfiable, so the plan must say whether a velocity key's result changes on an input change (and name the caller that spawns it) or only when its rounded window advances (and drop the velocity half of the fleet-event claim).
findings.text: §5 has `_serve_velocity` "spawn on a miss or a change" and line 136 push "a velocity key spanning every project" to every open stream as a `fleet` event, but line 138 rounds the key's window end down to the refresh interval so a stored result is "reused within that interval and recomputed after it" — a later interval yields a new key, not a changed one, so a given key's result is computed once and never changes — and the only change-spawner §5 names (line 137, `_FleetChangeWatch`) fires for the project discovery and the fleet rollup, never for a velocity key; the done-when's VelocityView assertion that it "re-requests when a `fleet` event names the key it shows" therefore exercises an event the production path never emits

response_events.reason: Deferred, not rejected: the finding holds. The fix is recorded as comment c-s5-velocity-event on section 5: a velocity key's event is published once, when its computation completes, and velocity drops 'on a change'. It is applied, with one review, when section 5 is next to build.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol §5 names resolves: `_start_check_refresh` / `_spawn_check_refresh` (`reckon/serve.py:3151` / `:3147`), `_CHECK_REFRESHES` (`:1474`), `Handler._send_project_changes` (`:3542`), `Handler._serve_velocity` (`:3631`), `compliance.project_checks` (`reckon/compliance.py:247`), `_FleetChangeWatch` (`reckon/serve.py:351`), `VelocityView` (`docs/ui/velocity.jsx:183`), `watchProjectStateChanges` (`docs/ui/state-loader.js:697`) and `tests/test_spa_crew_cards.py`; "§8's evidence" for 605.8 s resolves in the landed record, and `reckon/change_streams.py` is named as future ("once §16 lands"), not as present.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of the four route cases, the fleet-rollup case and the fleet-event case declares its own negative control, and the live measures are quantified (route answers under 50 ms while the stub runs; every derived endpoint under 1 s at the 95th percentile).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 inherits §2's log terms (logs under the run directory, ending in EXIT=, suite on the fleet allocation), so no gate lands in a scratchpad or a node-local temp tree.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the revision adds no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; the generic entries are named by function (compute, read the last result, spawn on change), and no comment needs a tracker entry to be read.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the velocity key makes a stored result immutable per rounded interval, so the fleet-event push for a velocity key has no production trigger and the caller that would spawn a velocity recompute on a change is unnamed.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: generalise the out-of-request recompute from one route to four, with the interface it names; the write paths are the files that one change touches.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5's declared depends-on [s3, s8] matches its own text ("Build it after §3 and §8 merge"), and §16 — which creates `reckon/change_streams.py`, a path §5 writes — is reached through §3's depends-on [s2, s14, s16].
